bug_info.bug_desc: The TPM `tpm_header_not_empty` interrupt was generated as a one-cycle pulse from a rising-edge detector on `tpm_status_cmdaddr_notempty`. Because the interrupt primitive received a pulse instead of the level status, software could clear the interrupt while the TPM command/address FIFO was still non-empty or while a new header arrived, losing the interrupt notification. This is a race condition in the interrupt handshake: the level status should be delivered directly to the interrupt logic so the interrupt remains asserted while the condition is true.
bug_info.fix_hint: Remove the edge detector and connect `tpm_status_cmdaddr_notempty` directly to the `event_intr_i` input of the `tpm_header_not_empty` interrupt primitive. Also delete the now-unused pulse signal declaration. This makes the interrupt level-sensitive with respect to the command/address FIFO not-empty status, preventing a software clear from losing a persistent nonempty condition. The interrupt state remains sticky after the FIFO drains until software clears it.
